newsitem.title: UK: U.S. scientists find special protein.
newsitem.headline: U.S. scientists find special protein.

text.p: Two teams of scientists in the United States reported on Monday they had found the protein that allows the body to absorb iron.
The protein also helps absorb other metals, such as zinc, copper, manganese and lead, the researchers said.

It could help doctors understand iron deficiency, or anaemia, as well as diseases such as hereditary haemochromatosis, which causes iron to build up in the liver, and other diseases of the brain and nervous system such as Parkinson's.

Matthias Hediger and colleagues at Brigham and Women's Hospital and Harvard Medical School in Boston examined a protein in rats called DCT1, which seems to help carry iron and other metals across cell membranes.
They also found the gene responsible for its production.

Large amounts are found in the duodenum, the part of the small intestine that absorbs metallic nutrients such as iron and zinc -- especially iron from vegetable sources such as leafy green vegetables.
Hediger's group tested rats and found when they were given an iron-deficient diet, DCT1 production was stepped up.
The protein could also play a role in the immune system, Hediger's group added in a report in the science journal Nature.
Nancy Andrews and her colleagues at Harvard made a similar discovery, reported in Nature's sister journal Nature Genetics.
They analysed mice that have anaemia due to a defect in intestinal iron absorption.
